property_summary: For any caller who is the owner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) never reverts and results in owner() == newOwner; the mutant that disallows transferring to the current owner will cause transferOwnership to revert when newOwner == owner(), violating this rule for those inputs.

For any caller who is the current owner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) either succeeds and updates owner() to newOwner (for all newOwner addresses) — the mutant that forbids transferring to the same owner will sometimes cause transferOwnership to revert when newOwner == owner(), violating the rule that owner() equals newOwner after a successful call (we assert success for all newOwner values, so the mutant will fail for the case newOwner == owner()).

For any caller who is the current owner and for any newOwner address, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) either (A) succeeds and afterwards owner() == newOwner, or (B) reverts; the reference contract never reverts when newOwner == owner() (it allows redundant transfers) while the mutant adds a require preventing transferring to the same owner and thus will revert for newOwner == owner(), so there exists an input (newOwner == current owner) where the mutant's call reverts but the reference's call would succeed — we assert that calling transferOwnership(newOwner) does not revert (ok==true) for all fuzzed newOwner when the caller is the current owner.

For any caller that is the current owner and any fuzzed target address newOwner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) should either succeed (and set owner() to newOwner) or revert; specifically, if the call succeeds then owner() must equal newOwner — the mutant adds a prohibition that makes calls where newOwner equals the current owner revert, so there exist fuzzed inputs (newOwner == current owner) where the mutant causes a revert but the reference would succeed and set owner unchanged.

For any caller that is the contract owner and any fuzzed address newOwner, calling transferOwnership(newOwner) on the correct contract always returns (does not revert) when invoked by the current owner (even if newOwner == owner()), while the mutant can revert for inputs where newOwner equals the current owner; we assert the call does not revert for all fuzzed newOwner addresses when invoked by the current owner.

Invariant: transferOwnership called by the current owner always succeeds (does not revert) for any nonzero newOwner and updates owner(); the mutant makes transferOwnership revert when owner was previously renounced (owner() == address(0)) because onlyOwner now requires owner() != address(0).

For any candidate newOwner and any caller, if transferOwnership is invoked by the current owner (owner() != address(0)) the call must succeed and update owner() to newOwner; the mutant additionally forbids calling owner-only functions once owner() has been renounced (owner()==address(0)), causing transferOwnership to revert in that state and thus violating the rule for some inputs.
